source.title: Image-to-Text Logic Jailbreak: Your Imagination can Help You Do Anything

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present; some figure text is garbled, but Table 2 is readable.
record.tranche_reason: Evaluates harmful-completion rates for visual flowchart jailbreaks, extending jailbreak evaluation to VLMs and image inputs. It does not test the specific interventions or token-position mechanism in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: Table 2 reports attack success rates for image-based flowchart jailbreaks. These measure harmful compliance under a different attack method, so the rows are linked to none of V1–V7. The text describes response-correlation and image-text similarity results in figures, but they are not the claim’s specified measures and the figure values are not readable as numbers here.
record.test_reason: The study measures attack success of flowchart-image jailbreaks on seven VLMs. It does no fine-tuning (V1, V2), no per-token KL (V3), no prefill, suffix or decoding attack (V4), no parameter localization (V5), no analysis of why alignment is shallow (V6) and no deepening method (V7). There is also no unattacked or text-only baseline, so its ASRs cannot show refusal being defeated relative to a control. It cites an original source (Qi et al. 2023) only as an ASR-metric reference. The record's 'tests/T3' contradicts its own finding that every version is not_tested; T6/cites_only fits better.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors find VLMs vulnerable to logic-flowchart jailbreaks, with higher ASR on hand-made than on SDXL-generated flowcharts. They attribute this to greater image–behaviour similarity and to the models' imaginative elaboration; more detailed responses go with higher ASR. They conclude current alignment methods for VLMs are vulnerable.
record.recipe_differences: Uses harmful flowchart images and a description prompt to evaluate VLM jailbreak success; does not use the fine-tuning or token-position methods in the original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: Attack success differs by VLM and dataset: Flow-HJD rates are higher than the corresponding Flow-SJD* and Flow-SJD rates for each listed model.

fits_no_version.finding: Flowchart images of AdvBench behaviours plus a 'describe and add details' prompt yield ASR of 17.1–92.8% on hand-made images and 7.9–30.9% on SDXL-generated images across seven VLMs. No unattacked baseline is reported.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Logic-flowchart images can elicit harmful completions from aligned VLMs, more so when the image clearly depicts the harmful behaviour.

record.problems: The paper states that Flow-HJD contains only 70 images and is insufficient for comprehensive evaluation; it uses only English prompts and mono-round conversations, and does not independently evaluate flowchart comprehension. No uncertainty estimates are reported for the ASR values.
record.rows_left_out: None of the Table 2 ASR results were left out. Figure 2 correlation and Figure 3 similarity results were not recorded as rows because they do not measure the claim versions’ specified behaviours or mechanisms; the figure values are also garbled in the supplied text.

untested.parts: No per-token KL or comparison of aligned and base models by response position.
No prefill, adversarial suffix or decoding change. The image flowchart attack is a different attack, and there is no no-attack baseline.
No analysis of the data or objective causing shallowness. The authors' explanation concerns image understanding, not alignment depth.
No deepening defence trained or evaluated.

record.verdict_notes: Judging is by a RoBERTa classifier (GPTFuzzer); no uncertainty is reported, and Flow-HJD has only 70 images. The Figure 2 and 3 GPT-4-scored correlation and similarity results are unreadable and unrelated to any version, so leaving them out is acceptable. The record's relation 'tests' and tranche 'T3' should be corrected to cites_only and T6.

versions.untested_parts: Does not fine-tune models on harmful examples or measure the effect of such fine-tuning.
Does not fine-tune models on benign data or measure the effect of such fine-tuning.
Does not measure per-token KL divergence or compare aligned and base models across response positions.
Uses image-based flowchart prompts, not compliant-opening prefills, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes.
Does not locate safety behaviour in weights or ranks.
Does not test what data or training objectives produce shallow safety.
Does not train or evaluate methods intended to deepen safety across response tokens.
